title: Your App Demo Only Sells in English — That's Leaving Money on the Table
description: A product demo video is your best salesperson. Keeping it in one language caps your app's reach. Dubbing unlocks every market at once.
excerpt: Your demo video does the selling while you sleep — but only for people who speak its language. Dubbing lets it sell everywhere.
content:
A good product demo is the hardest-working asset a software company has. It sits on your landing page, in your app store listing, in ads and onboarding, and it sells around the clock. But if it only speaks one language, it only sells to one slice of your potential users.

**Global downloads, single-language demo**

App stores are global by default. Someone in Brazil, Poland, or Japan can install your app today. But your demo — the thing that turns a curious visitor into a user — talks to them in a language they may barely follow. Subtitles help a little, but for a fast product walkthrough they split attention exactly when you need it focused.

**Dub the demo, widen the funnel**

[TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs your product video into 50+ languages while keeping your narrator's voice and timing. The same crisp walkthrough now explains your app in the viewer's language, on your localized landing pages and store listings.

**Cheap reach from work you already did**

You already paid to script, record, and edit the demo. Dubbing multiplies its reach for a fraction of that cost — no reshoot, no new voice actors per market. For a SaaS or app business, a demo that converts in ten languages instead of one is one of the highest-leverage moves available.

**Where to start**

Dub your main demo into the two or three languages where you already see signups or traffic but weaker conversion. Put the localized versions on matching landing pages. Watch whether conversion rises when visitors finally understand the pitch.

Your demo is already built. Dub it, and it starts selling in every market you ship to.
